lifecycle_alerts.description: Whether the channel also takes spend and lifecycle warnings. Default true.

min_severity.description: The lowest severity the channel takes: low, medium, high or critical. Default medium.

name.description: 1 to 63 of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit, unique among channels not removed.

url.description: Where alerts go: a Slack incoming-webhook address, or the webhook's. It is https, or http to this machine. kman seals it and never shows it again.

name.description: 1 to 63 of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit, unique among credentials not deleted.

secret.description: The real secret. kman seals it and never shows it again. For basic auth without a username, the whole user:password.

key.description: The key id it applies to. Absent: every key. A canary has none.

label.description: What it is, 1 to 64 characters with no control characters.

value.description: cidr: a network no wider than an IPv4 /16 or an IPv6 /32, or one address. country: two capital letters. asn: a number, with or without AS. client: a product and major version as events record it, such as curl/8; none and unknown are refused, since they would silence every request that does not say what it is.

auth.description: A custom upstream defaults to Authorization: Bearer {key}, or x-api-key: {key} on the anthropic profile.

credential.description: A first credential, added in the same transaction: a bad secret adds no upstream either.

host.description: A host name or IP address, with no scheme, port or path. A custom upstream needs one.

name.description: 1 to 63 of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit. With a preset, it defaults to the preset's name.

path_allowlist.description: The rules a request must match, as METHOD /path. A custom upstream needs at least one; * /** allows everything.

port.description: A custom upstream defaults to 443 with TLS and 80 without.

preset.description: The preset to copy. Absent to build a custom upstream from the settings.

price_multiplier_ppm.description: What built-in prices and install-wide overrides are multiplied by on this upstream, in parts per million, for a regional uplift: 1000000 is x1, the default, and 1100000 is x1.1. Above 0, up to x100. It does not touch a per-upstream override or a cost the provider reports.

profile.description: openai, anthropic or generic. A custom upstream defaults to generic.

server_name.description: The TLS server name, when it is not the host.

tls.description: A custom upstream defaults to true.

last_used_at.description: When the token last authenticated a request, to the minute. Absent if never.

name.description: The token's name, which is the actor of every change made with it.

revoked_at.description: When the token was revoked. Absent while it is live.

actor.description: Who made the change: an admin token's name, or system:<what> for kman itself.

after.description: The target after the change, where the action records it. Never a secret.

before.description: The target before the change, where the action records it. Never a secret.

id.description: Rising with each entry; the cursor for paging.

more.description: Whether the log holds more entries beyond this page: after it, or before it with latest.

basic_username.description: For the basic style, the username. When absent, a credential's secret is the whole user:password.

header.description: For the header style, the template: Name: value {key}.

armed_at.description: When it was made or last reset.

fired_at.description: The first use since it was armed. Absent while it is armed.

fires.description: How many uses were counted since the canary was made, from addresses not on its ignore list.

id.description: The key id: the non-secret handle inside the canary's key, and how this API addresses it. It is the id the canary's alerts and its events name.

ignore.description: Addresses and networks whose use does not fire it, such as the operator's own scanners. The use is still an event.

last_fired_at.description: The last use. A reset keeps it.

last_use.description: Where the last use came from.

name.description: An optional label, unique among keys not revoked.

planted.description: Where it was planted, in the operator's words: what an alert says so that the leak can be found.

state.description: armed: its next use raises an alert. fired: it was used since it was armed, so more uses count and only now and then alert again, until it is reset. revoked: it is over and answers key_revoked.

address.description: The client address. Left out unless the expose_client_addresses setting is on.

address_withheld.description: There is an address, which is left out because expose_client_addresses is off.

as_org.description: The organisation the ASN belongs to, when the ASN database names one.

client.description: What called: the User-Agent reduced to a product and major version, such as curl/8, or none.

country.description: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, when a GeoIP database names one.

ignore.description: The new ignore list, which replaces the old one; empty clears it.

planted.description: A new place it was planted.

tags.description: The new tags, which replace the old ones.

delivered.description: How many alerts it has been sent, until they are pruned.

failed.description: How many alerts were given up on.

host.description: The host of its address, which is all of the address that is shown.

last_error.description: Why the latest failed attempt failed. Never the address.

lifecycle_alerts.description: Whether it also takes spend and lifecycle warnings.

min_severity.description: The lowest severity it takes: low, medium, high or critical.

pending.description: How many alerts wait in the outbox for it.

error.description: Why the test alert did not arrive. Never the address.

incident_id.description: The incident this is done for. It must exist, be unresolved and be about a key on this credential. The compromise and that key's rotation are audited with its id, and it is resolved as confirmed.

secret.description: The new real secret, made at the provider after the leaked one was revoked there. kman seals it and never shows it again.

rotated_keys.description: Every virtual key on the credential that was not revoked, oldest first, with its new secret, shown only this once. Each is an app that needs its new key.

incident_id.description: The incident this is done for. It must exist, be about this key and be unresolved. The audit entry carries its id, so the incident's timeline shows the action. Disabling leaves the incident open; revoking resolves it as confirmed.

name.description: 1 to 63 of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit. A revoked token's name stays taken.

base_url.description: kman's proxy URL, as an app would be told it. When given, the snippet sets the variable's base URL too, so a thief who finds the snippet alone can reach kman with it.

format.description: The snippet to plant: env (a .env line), mcp (an MCP server config's env block), shell (an export line) or ci (a gh secret set command). Defaults to env.

ignore.description: Addresses and networks (CIDR) whose use does not fire the canary. At most 100, none wider than an IPv4 /16 or an IPv6 /32.

name.description: An optional label: 1 to 63 of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit, unique among keys not revoked. It stays out of the snippet.

planted.description: Where it will be planted: 1 to 200 characters, with no control characters. An alert names it.

tags.description: At most 32 labels of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_', ':' and '-'.

var.description: The variable the snippet sets, such as OPENAI_API_KEY (the default). A thief finds a key by the name it is under.

credential.description: The credential's name or id. Needed when the upstream has more than one.

name.description: An optional label: 1 to 63 of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit, unique among keys not revoked.

note.description: Free text of at most 1024 bytes, with no control characters.

policy.description: The key's policy, a JSON object. Defaults to the empty policy.

tags.description: At most 32 labels of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_', ':' and '-'.

ttl_seconds.description: How long the key stays valid from now, at most the maximum key lifetime. Defaults to the default key TTL.

secret.description: The token itself (kma_...). kman keeps only its hash, so it is shown only this once.
The canary's key (kmn_...), in the standard format: nothing in it says it is a canary. kman keeps only its hash, so it is shown only this once.

snippet.description: What to plant, in the format asked for. It holds the secret, so it is shown only this once, and it says nothing of what it is: not the canary's name, where it is planted, or its tags.

signing_secret.description: For a webhook, the secret that signs each request (kmwhsec_...), shown only this once. A receiver recomputes the signature with it.

sdk_base_path.description: Appended to kman's proxy URL to make an SDK's base URL.

sdk_env.description: The variable an SDK for its upstream reads the key from.

secret.description: The virtual key itself (kmn_...). kman keeps only its hash, so it is shown only this once.

last4.description: The end of the secret, to tell credentials apart. Absent for a secret too short to show any of.

rotated_at.description: When the secret was last replaced.

secret.description: A new secret, which overwrites the old one. The credential keeps its id, so virtual keys on it are not touched.

asn.description: The autonomous system number, from the ASN database, when there is one that knows the address.

asn_label.description: The autonomous system's organisation, when the ASN database names one.

client.description: What made the request: its User-Agent reduced to a product and major version, such as openai-python/3 or curl/8, or none when it sent no User-Agent. Never the header itself. Empty for an event stored before kman recorded it. It is not personal data, so it is always shown.

client_address.description: The client address: the connection's, or X-Forwarded-For only through trusted_proxies. Left out unless the expose_client_addresses setting is on.

client_address_withheld.description: The event has a client address, which is left out because expose_client_addresses is off.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 code, from the country database, when there is one that knows the address.

id.description: The stored event's id, which pages by. Not set on an event from the live stream, which is not stored yet.

key_id.description: The virtual key's id. Empty when the request presented no key that kman could identify.

kind.description: forwarded: kman sent the request to an upstream, or it was a realtime session. refused: kman answered it itself, with a refusal code.

operation.description: The request's method and path, such as POST /v1/chat/completions. Never a query string.

refusal_code.description: The error code of a refusal, such as key_disabled or invalid_key.

status.description: The status the app was sent.

unidentified_key.description: The request presented no key that kman could identify: a key that does not exist, or none. Many of these from one place is probing.

client_addresses_withheld.description: Client addresses were left out because expose_client_addresses is off.

more.description: Whether there are older events that match.

next_before.description: The id to send as before for the next, older page. Set when more is true.

keys_checked.description: How many keys were looked at: the keys that work now. A disabled, revoked or expired key cannot be abused, and a canary is meant to be left alone.

fix.description: The kman command that fixes it, ready to run. An open key's has a placeholder to replace with the network the key is used from.

last_used_at.description: For unused: the start of the last hour in which the key forwarded a request. Absent if it never has.

detection_count.description: Every detection raised, repeats included. The detail lists the first 100 of them.

id.description: A plain integer, as alerts and commands name it.

quiet.description: Nothing has fired for an hour. Display only: the incident is still unresolved, and a new firing on a quiet incident alerts again.

resolved_by.description: An admin token's name, or system:detect when it expired.

rules.description: The rules that have fired, in the order they first did.

severity.description: low, medium, high or critical: the highest of its detections.

actions.description: The audit entries that carry the incident's id: its opening and escalations by system:detect, and what operators did about it. With the detections, the timeline.

addresses_withheld.description: A client address or network was left out of the evidence because expose_client_addresses is off.

detection_count.description: Every detection raised, repeats included. The detail lists the first 100 of them.

detections.description: What fired, oldest first, at most 100.

id.description: A plain integer, as alerts and commands name it.

known_source_candidates.description: The places the detections saw, which this was me can add as known sources. None for a canary.

quiet.description: Nothing has fired for an hour. Display only: the incident is still unresolved, and a new firing on a quiet incident alerts again.

resolved_by.description: An admin token's name, or system:detect when it expired.

rules.description: The rules that have fired, in the order they first did.

severity.description: low, medium, high or critical: the highest of its detections.

address.description: The client address. Left out unless expose_client_addresses is on.

address_withheld.description: There is an address or network, which is left out because expose_client_addresses is off.

client.description: What called: the User-Agent reduced to a product and major version.

network.description: The network (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /64). Left out unless expose_client_addresses is on.

observed.description: What the rule saw, for a rule that compares: a rate, a spend, a place.

more.description: There are older incidents beyond this page: pass the last id as before.

credential.description: The credential's name. Absent once a revoked key's credential is deleted.

expired.description: Whether its expiry has passed, whatever its status.

expires_at.description: When the key stops working. Every key has one: there is no never. A canary has none, and shows the zero time.

id.description: The key id: the non-secret handle inside the key, and how this API addresses it.

kind.description: standard, or canary: a key with no credential that forwards nothing and raises an alert when used. A canary is not in the list of keys; GET /canaries lists them.

name.description: An optional label, unique among keys not revoked.

policy.description: The key's policy, a JSON object: empty until it is edited.

policy_version.description: The version of the policy format the policy is in.

spend.description: What the key has spent today and this month, beside its caps. Shown when the key is read, and not in the audit log.

upstream.description: The upstream's name. Absent once a revoked key's upstream is deleted.

address.description: The client address: the connection's, or X-Forwarded-For only through trusted_proxies.

asn.description: The autonomous system number, from the ASN database, when there is one that knows the address.

blocked.description: Requests kman refused: a locked address, a refused key, a policy.

cost_micro.description: The known cost of its requests, in microdollars.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 code, from the country database, when there is one that knows the address.

unmetered_requests.description: Forwarded requests whose cost is not known, which cost_micro does not include.

clients.description: The addresses the key was used from, the most recently seen first, at most 50. A request that came in on a Unix socket has no address and is not counted.

total.description: How many distinct addresses the key was used from. More than the length of clients when the list was cut.

networks_withheld.description: Network places were left out because expose_client_addresses is off.

name.description: A new name, or empty for none.

note.description: A new note, or empty for none.

policy.description: The new policy, a JSON object, which replaces the old one.

tags.description: The new tags, which replace the old ones.

ttl_seconds.description: A new expiry, this long from now. It may not be later than the key's creation plus the maximum key lifetime, unless that shortens the key's life.

scope.description: The key id it applies to. Empty: every key.

value.description: A network in CIDR form, an ISO 3166-1 country code, an AS number without the AS, or a client (a User-Agent reduced to a product and major version, such as curl/8).
The value to add. Empty for a network while expose_client_addresses is off.

secret.description: The real secret. kman seals it and never shows it again. For basic auth without a username, the whole user:password.

label.description: A name for the value, when kman has one: an AS's organisation, from the ASN database.

other.description: This row counts every place of its kind past the first 1,000 the key was seen from.

requests.description: Requests kman forwarded from here, and realtime sessions.

value.description: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, an AS number, an IPv4 /24 or IPv6 /64 network, or a client: the User-Agent reduced to a product and major version, such as openai-python/3, or none. Empty for the other row.

notice.description: What to tell the operator when it is stale.

stale.description: Whether the table is past 60 days old.

models.description: The built-in entries. An override below may hide one.

overrides.description: The price overrides, which win over the built-in entries until removed.

audio_input_micro.description: Audio input. Absent: billed at the input price.

audio_output_micro.description: Audio output. Absent: billed at the output price.

cache_write_micro.description: Cache writes. Absent: billed at the input price.

cached_micro.description: Cached input. Absent: billed at the input price.

long_context.description: Prices for a whole request whose input is over a size.

max_output.description: The most tokens one response can output, which sizes reservations.

mode.description: chat, responses, completion, embedding or realtime.

per_minute_micro.description: Voice: per minute, billed per second.

preset.description: The preset this entry belongs to. Absent for a global entry, which every upstream falls back to.

reviewed.description: Whether a person checked max_output against the provider's docs.

service_tiers.description: The service tiers with their own prices.

audio_cached_micro.description: Cached audio input. Absent: billed at the audio input price.

audio_input_micro.description: Audio input. Absent: billed at the input price.

audio_output_micro.description: Audio output. Absent: billed at the output price.

cache_write_1h_micro.description: One-hour cache writes. Absent: billed at the cache write price.

cache_write_micro.description: Cache writes. Absent: billed at the input price.

cached_micro.description: Cached input. Absent: billed at the input price.

hides.description: The sections of the price table whose built-in entry for this model it hides: global or a preset's name.

max_output.description: The most tokens one response can output, which sizes reservations.

upstream.description: The upstream it applies to, by name. Absent for an install-wide override.

changed.description: How many it added or changed, each with its own audit entry.

overrides.description: Every override it named, as it now stands.

unchanged.description: How many already had these prices.

audio_cached_micro.description: Cached audio input. Absent: billed at the audio input price.

audio_input_micro.description: Audio input. Absent: billed at the input price.

audio_output_micro.description: Audio output. Absent: billed at the output price.

cache_write_1h_micro.description: One-hour cache writes. Absent: billed at the cache write price.

cache_write_micro.description: Cache writes. Absent: billed at the input price.

cached_micro.description: Cached input. Absent: billed at the input price.

input_micro.description: Input, in microdollars per million tokens.

max_output.description: The most tokens one response can output, which sizes reservations.

output_micro.description: Output, in microdollars per million tokens.

upstream.description: The upstream to price it on, by name or id. Absent for the whole install.

audit_log.description: Also delete the audit log's entries older than before. The one thing that ever deletes from the audit log. The prune is recorded in the log, and that record stays.

before.description: Delete what is older than this: events, hourly usage, and alerts delivered before it. Not in the future.

audit_entries.description: Audit log entries deleted. 0 unless audit_log was set.

delivered_alerts.description: Alerts deleted that were delivered before the date. Pending and failed alerts are kept.

hourly_usage.description: Hourly usage rows deleted: those whose hour ended before the date.

as.description: confirmed (the default) or false_positive (false-positive is accepted). A false positive lets what the incident held out of the key's baseline back in, so it is the operator's call. expired is only ever set by kman.

grace_seconds.description: How long the old secret keeps working beside the new one, at most 30 days. Absent or 0 ends it at once, on the next request.

incident_id.description: The incident this is done for. It must exist, be about this key and be unresolved. The rotation is audited with its id and resolves it as confirmed.

key.description: The same key, with the same id, spend, policy and history: only its secret is new.

previous_valid_until.description: When the old secret stops working. Absent when it stopped at once.

sdk_env.description: The variable an SDK for its upstream reads the key from.

secret.description: The new virtual key (kmn_...). kman keeps only its hash, so it is shown only this once.

default_key_ttl_seconds.description: How long a new virtual key stays valid unless told otherwise. At most the maximum key lifetime. Default 90 days.

expose_client_addresses.description: Whether the admin API may tell which client addresses used a key (GET /keys/{id}/clients), the networks a key was used from (GET /keys/{id}/places), and the client address of each event (GET /events and its stream). Off by default: an address is personal data, and it stays out of the API until an operator turns it on. Turning it on and off is audited.

max_key_lifetime_seconds.description: The longest any virtual key may stay valid. No key is created or extended past it. Default 365 days.

soft_budget_defaults.description: The percentages of each spend cap or soft budget that raise a warning when crossed, rising, for keys whose policy sets none (soft_budget_percents). Each warns once per day or month. Default 50, 80, 100; an empty list warns for no key that sets none. A change takes effect at the next check, within a minute.

spend_timezone.description: The IANA time zone in which daily and monthly spend periods start at 00:00. Default UTC. A change takes effect when kman restarts.

cap_micro.description: The key's cap for the period, in microdollars. Absent for none.

cost_micro.description: What has been charged, in microdollars, estimated_micro included.

estimated_micro.description: The part of cost_micro charged as an estimate: the whole reservation, for a response that was cut off or reported no usage.

period.description: The day, such as 2026-11-11, or the month, such as 2026-11.

reserved_micro.description: Held for requests in flight. A cap counts it as it counts cost_micro.

unmetered_requests.description: Requests forwarded that could not be metered, whose cost is unknown and so is not in cost_micro.

add_known_sources.description: Also add the places the incident saw as known sources, so they stop counting as new. Never for a canary.

install_wide.description: Add them for every key, not just this one. Needs add_known_sources.

kinds.description: Add only these kinds: country, asn, client, network. Default all. Needs add_known_sources.

label.description: The label for the known sources. Default says which incident they came from. Needs add_known_sources.

already_known.description: Places that were already known sources in that scope, so none was added.

withheld_networks.description: Networks that were not added, because adding one would give it out while expose_client_addresses is off.

available.description: Whether Latest is newer than Current.

checked_at.description: When the last check ran, successful or not.

current.description: This binary's version, such as v0.1.0, or empty for a build that is not a release.

enabled.description: Whether update_check is on in kman.yaml. kman asks the GitHub releases API once a day only when it is.

error.description: Why the last check failed, if it did. Latest is still what an earlier check found.

latest.description: The newest release the last successful check found.

url.description: The page of the latest release.

credentials.description: Its credentials, by name. Never a secret.

path_allowlist.description: The rules a request must match, as METHOD /path: * is any method or one segment, and a last segment of ** is the rest of the path.

preset.description: The preset it was copied from. Absent for a custom upstream.

preset_version.description: The version of the preset it was last copied from.

price_multiplier_ppm.description: What built-in prices and install-wide overrides are multiplied by on this upstream, in parts per million: 1000000 is x1.

sdk_base_path.description: Appended to kman's proxy URL to make an SDK's base URL.

sdk_env.description: The variable an SDK for this upstream reads its key from.

server_name.description: The TLS server name, when it is not the host.

update_available.description: Whether this kman holds a newer version of the preset: see the sync operation.

field.description: The upstream's field, by its name in the API.

from.description: What it holds now. Absent if nothing.

to.description: What the sync would set. Absent if nothing.

changes.description: What the sync would change, which undoes any edit made since the last copy. Empty when up to date, and possibly when only the version moves.

from_version.description: The version of the preset the upstream was last copied from.

generation.description: The upstream's generation: pass it to the sync, which refuses if the upstream has changed since.

to_version.description: The version of the preset this kman holds.

up_to_date.description: Whether this kman holds no newer version, so there is nothing to sync.

auth.description: A custom upstream defaults to Authorization: Bearer {key}, or x-api-key: {key} on the anthropic profile.

host.description: A host name or IP address, with no scheme, port or path. A custom upstream needs one.

path_allowlist.description: The rules a request must match, as METHOD /path. A custom upstream needs at least one; * /** allows everything.

port.description: A custom upstream defaults to 443 with TLS and 80 without.

price_multiplier_ppm.description: What built-in prices and install-wide overrides are multiplied by on this upstream, in parts per million, for a regional uplift: 1000000 is x1, the default, and 1100000 is x1.1. Above 0, up to x100. It does not touch a per-upstream override or a cost the provider reports.

profile.description: openai, anthropic or generic. A custom upstream defaults to generic.

server_name.description: The TLS server name, when it is not the host.

tls.description: A custom upstream defaults to true.

actor.description: The name of the admin token the request was made with.

adminToken.description: An admin token (kma_...). A dashboard session cookie is never accepted here.

info.description: The one way to change a running kman (ADR 0004). Every change is one store transaction, audited with its actor: the name of the admin token the request was made with. Generated from the Go types in internal/admin; do not edit by hand.

parameters.description: Only events of this kind: forwarded or refused.
parameters.name: kind

parameters.description: Only events with this refusal code, such as invalid_key.
parameters.name: code

200.description: A stream of server-sent events that lasts until the client leaves. Each message's data is one Event as JSON; an event: dropped message says how many events this client has missed, as {"missed": n}; lines that start with a colon are keep-alives.

get.summary: Follow new events as they happen, as server-sent events, with the filters of the list. A client that cannot keep up loses events and is told how many
List the keys that work now and would be easy to abuse: open to every address, never expiring, or unused for 30 days, each with the command that fixes it

parameters.description: Only incidents that are not resolved.
parameters.name: open

parameters.description: Only this key's incidents, by key id.
parameters.name: key

parameters.description: Only incidents with an id below this: the cursor for paging.
parameters.name: before

parameters.description: The most incidents to return, 1 to 500. Default 50.
parameters.name: limit

get.summary: List incidents, newest first: the open case for each key whose rules fired, with its state, severity, rules and how many detections it has; filtered by open, and key, and paged

Read one incident with its detections and the actions taken on it, which are its timeline, and the places it saw that this was me could add as known sources. A client address or network in the evidence is left out unless the expose_client_addresses setting is on

post.summary: Acknowledge an incident: its repeats stop alerting, and an escalation still alerts
Resolve an incident as confirmed (the default) or false_positive
Resolve an incident as a false positive and, if asked, add the places it saw as known sources, for its key or for every key. Never for a canary

parameters.description: Only the key not revoked with this name.
parameters.name: name

get.summary: List every virtual key, or the one with a name, never their secrets

post.summary: Create a virtual key on an upstream; its secret is returned only this once

get.summary: Read one virtual key, by key id

patch.summary: Change a virtual key's name, note, tags, expiry or policy

get.summary: List the client addresses a virtual key was used from, grouped, from the events kept; refused unless the expose_client_addresses setting is on

post.summary: Stop a virtual key from the next request until it is enabled again
Let a disabled virtual key work again; a revoked key cannot be enabled

parameters.description: Only places of this kind: country, asn, network or client.
parameters.name: kind

get.summary: List where a virtual key has been used from: each country, AS and network, and each client (the User-Agent reduced to a product and major version) that used it, with when it was first and last seen and how many requests were forwarded and refused

post.summary: End a virtual key for good, from the next request; it cannot be undone
Replace a virtual key's secret and keep the key; the new secret is returned only this once

parameters.description: Only those that apply to this key, by key id: the install-wide ones and its own.
parameters.name: key

get.summary: List the known sources: labelled networks, countries, ASNs and clients the operator says are legitimate, for every key or one. They never silence a canary

post.summary: Add a known source: a labelled CIDR, country, ASN or client, for every key or one

get.summary: This document. It needs no admin token.

parameters.description: The upstream it is on, by name or id. Absent for an install-wide override.
parameters.name: upstream

put.summary: Set a price override, install-wide or on one upstream; it wins over the built-in entries until removed

post.summary: Set many price overrides, all or none

parameters.description: Only this preset's entries, or global for the global ones, and the overrides that reach them: install-wide ones and those on an upstream built from it.
parameters.name: preset

parameters.description: Only models whose id contains this, in any case. It narrows the overrides too.
parameters.name: model

get.summary: List the built-in price table, how old it is, and the price overrides
Say how old the built-in price table is, and whether to upgrade

post.summary: Delete events, hourly usage and delivered alerts older than a date, and with audit_log the audit log's entries too; the prune is audited

get.summary: Read the install's settings

patch.summary: Change some settings; each change is audited

get.summary: Say whether a newer kman release is known; only an install with update_check on ever asks
List every upstream with its credentials, never their secrets

post.summary: Add an upstream, copying a preset or built from the settings

delete.summary: Delete an upstream, its credentials and its price overrides; refused while a virtual key that is not revoked depends on one

get.summary: Read one upstream, by name or id

patch.summary: Change some of an upstream's settings

get.summary: Show how an upstream differs from a newer version of its preset, changing nothing

post.summary: Apply a sync plan; refused if the upstream or the preset has moved since

get.summary: Name the admin token this request is made with
